GENERALISABLE_DEFECT_CLASSES_FOR_THE_BUI: Four findings that are not product-specific and should be added to templates/PRODUCT_BUILD_GUIDE.md. (1) pytest.approx(expected, rel=r) carries a DEFAULT ABSOLUTE TOLERANCE of 1e-12 and passes on EITHER bound, so for any quantity of order 1e-5 every relative tolerance tighter than 2e-8 is silently replaced by it. P076 found this by re-running its whole suite with abs=0.0 substituted into all 95 rel= calls: exactly 3 of 271 assertions depended on the default, and one of them was hiding a real 2.086218e-10 relative discrepancy. (2) A validation check comparing a computed quantity against an INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED BOUND caught catastrophic cancellation in P077's closed form that 777 tests including property tests could not, because the tests compared the series against expressions sharing the same cancellation. That is a distinct check class from 'two implementations agree'. (3) Injecting a bound violation by OFFSETTING the reconstruction does not guarantee a violation - only an offset strictly greater than twice the bound does, since the reconstruction already sits inside the band. P080 had two of eleven negative controls silently too weak; the certificate was right and the control was wrong. Anchor controls on the true value. (4) An under-strength analytic baseline inflated P077's apparent learned-model win by about 50 per cent; validate the baseline against the simulation BEFORE benchmarking the model.
